rv.q: I particularly liked his lightning impression of Groucho in his "Hello, I must be going" mode. In the end, there is something sentimental in Odets's view of what constitutes great acting: when Frank strikes a fellow actor on stage, we're meant to admire his feral instinct instead of deploring his lack of professionalism.
This is a wonderful play, about acting and the theatre, deception and love, and it deserves to hit home harder and to be “voiced” more gorgeously.

But a young, ambitious director, Bernie Dodd thinks Elgin can be the key to the success of a new play and wants him for a comeback. At the heart of the struggle between the two men is Elgin’s long-suffering wife Georgie. What takes place is a fierce tug-of-war between this enigmatic woman and the hot-headed Dodd.
